items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: So I ran into Teddy Reig one day. So we got to talking about Bird.

ctx.x: So I became very curious about this cat, because he was so beautiful as a person. I mean he showed such great compassion and such true concern, beyond all the other musicians that I had met. And I was wondering, this guy, there’s more to him than meets the eye. Then I used to hang out uptown with the songwriters on 50th Street and Broadway. So I ran into Teddy Reig one day. So we got to talking about Bird. Teddy Reig used to sell bass drum beaters. That was his thing that he sold. And he made the first records…

without any hesitation, Bird says, “change the title, just call it “Ko-Ko.’” He says, “Cocoa, you mean the drink?” He says, “no ‘Ko-Ko.’” And you think that’ll work? Bird says, “why not?” You know the melody isn’t defined anywhere. So they did it, and it was a big hit. And then Teddy Reig says, 20 years later he realized that “Ko-Ko” was the lord high executioner in the mythical kingdom of Titipu in Gilbert & Sullivan’s “The Mikado,” which took place in Mongolia.
